per_claim.claim: SPLIT operator (Sec 3.1, Eqs 4–5) converts 1 parent into parent+2 children while conserving mass/weight exactly (parent W -= 2*Wchild).
per_claim.note: Unit tests over 20000 random splits show zero relative mass error.

per_claim.claim: SPLIT conserves center-of-mass/charge via symmetric displacement.
per_claim.note: Max relative COM error ~2.9e-16, consistent with floating-point roundoff.

per_claim.claim: SPLIT conserves total energy (KE + q*Phi) by correcting the field-parallel child velocity for displacement through the element E-field; rejects energetically inaccessible (imaginary-velocity) splits.
per_claim.note: Energy conserved to ~4.4e-16 in constant-element-field setting; imaginary-velocity cases correctly rejected.

per_claim.claim: MERGE operator (Sec 3.2, Eqs 6–12) converts 2 particles into 1 at their COM, conserving mass (Wmerge=W1+W2).
per_claim.note: Zero relative mass error in ~18600 merges.

per_claim.claim: MERGE conserves momentum at the COM (Eq 10).
MERGE intentionally loses a nonnegative amount of thermal kinetic energy (Eq 11, KElost>=0), with merges gated by cutoffs (Eq 9: dv<vthermal, alpha<30deg).
per_claim.note: KElost was never negative (18612/18612), and 1388 candidate pairs were rejected by the stated cutoffs.

per_claim.claim: MERGE thermal-energy loss is 'small' in accepted merges (bounded by the cutoffs).
per_claim.note: Replicator reports small losses (median 0.062%, 95th 0.587%) under the cutoffs, consistent qualitatively, but the paper’s quantitative distribution/targets are not fully reproduced/compared.

per_claim.claim: Numerical demo Test 4.1: reweighted VDFs are indistinguishable from fixed-weight in the exponential sheath case.
per_claim.note: Only operator-level conservation tests were run using the sheath field; no full PIC/sheath transient or VDF comparison to fixed-weight was reproduced.

per_claim.claim: Numerical demo Test 4.2: in 0D H2 ionization growth, real electron count grows at ~3.06 s^-1 independent of target computational particle count Nc, while computational count remains bounded near Nc (~Nc to 1.1*Nc), and fitted-rate precision improves with Nc.
per_claim.note: Independence of fitted growth rate across Nc and bounded computational count were reproduced in an abstracted 0D bookkeeping model; DSMC/cross-section physics and the 'precision improves with Nc' sub-claim were not reproduced.

justification: The reimplementation convincingly reproduces the core mathematical/structural properties of the split and merge operators: mass/COM/momentum conservation, energy-conserving split with rejection of inaccessible splits, and nonnegative (typically small) merge energy loss under the stated cutoffs. It also reproduces the key structural claim from Test 4.2 that the real-particle growth rate can be independent of Nc while keeping computational counts bounded, albeit in an abstracted model. However, the paper’s main end-to-end PIC/DSMC demonstration claims (VDF indistinguishability in Test 4.1 and physics-faithful 0D H2 ionization behavior including precision-vs-Nc) were not replicated. Thus the reproduction supports the operator correctness and one central scaling behavior, but not the full demonstrated simulation outcomes.
